topic: DDR4 versus DDR5 in four rounds
title: Spec Duel: DDR4 vs DDR5 in Four Rounds #siliconverdict #ddr5 #specduel
description: DDR4 and DDR5 compared in four rounds: data rate, bandwidth, voltage and lanes per stick.
pinned_comment: DDR4 or DDR5? Reply with one word.

scenes.narration: DDR5 is not just faster. It does something DDR4 never could.
Four rounds, same memory, and the last round has a catch.
Round one, speed. Standard DDR4 starts at thirty-two hundred transfers a second, DDR5 at forty-eight hundred.
That works out to about twenty-five point six gigabytes a second for DDR4, and thirty-eight point four for DDR5.
Round two, power. DDR5 runs at one point one volts, DDR4 at one point two, so lower wins.
Two rounds done, and the next one is the one most people miss.
Round three, capacity. The biggest sticks you can easily buy are roughly thirty-two gigabytes for DDR4 and sixty-four for DDR5.
Here is the twist: each DDR5 stick is split into two independent thirty-two bit lanes.
Round four, lanes per stick: DDR4 has one, DDR5 has two, which keeps the processor busier.
DDR5 wins on paper, but only if your motherboard and processor support it.
Higher speed also means higher latency numbers, so real gains are smaller than the headline.
Follow for more. Are you team DDR4 or team DDR5?
